name: Theophylline mesotherapy

card.summary: Injections of the methylxanthine theophylline into fat, used in lipolytic mesotherapy cocktails with the aim of reducing small fat deposits.
card.note: Theophylline has a narrow therapeutic window; it is a prescription drug.

quick.overview:
Theophylline mesotherapy refers to the use of theophylline, a methylxanthine related to caffeine, in small injections into the skin and fat layer. It is one of the agents used in lipolytic mesotherapy, a cosmetic approach aimed at slimming localized fat such as under the chin or on the thighs.
The idea is that theophylline raises cAMP inside cells, a signal tied to fat breakdown. Practitioners offering such treatments say it can reduce small pockets of fat; no trial has tested it for this purpose.
quick.how: Mesotherapy is delivered by a clinician as a series of microinjections into the target area. Theophylline is typically one component of a mixed preparation. Details of formulas and amounts are set by the prescriber and are not covered here.
quick.risks: Theophylline is a prescription asthma and COPD drug with a narrow therapeutic window: side effects include nausea, fast heart rate, headache and insomnia, and toxicity can cause arrhythmias and seizures. It interacts with several antibiotics and fluvoxamine. Injection treatments carry the general risks of injections.

lead: Theophylline (1,3-dimethylxanthine) is a methylxanthine, related to caffeine, that is used in medicine for asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease [1]. In aesthetic medicine it is also named as a component of lipolytic mesotherapy, in which small injections are given into subcutaneous fat to reduce localized deposits.

Its proposed role follows from pharmacology: theophylline is a non-selective phosphodiesterase inhibitor, which raises intracellular cAMP and cGMP, and it blocks adenosine receptors [1]. Those cAMP-raising effects are the rationale offered for fat-breakdown (lipolysis) in fat cells.
The medical-use pages consulted do not discuss cosmetic or lipolytic use, and no published trial has been identified for theophylline mesotherapy in this review.

chain: Claimed fat breakdown and smaller local deposit
angle.text: Clinics that offer lipolytic mesotherapy use theophylline-containing mixtures with the aim of contouring small areas such as the chin or thighs.

paras: Theophylline inhibits phosphodiesterases, raising cAMP and cGMP, and antagonizes adenosine A1, A2 and A3 receptors [1].

Reported effects include nausea, diarrhea, faster heart rate, rhythm abnormalities, headache, insomnia and irritability, and severe toxicity can cause seizures. The drug has a narrow therapeutic window, and erythromycin, cimetidine, fluoroquinolones and fluvoxamine raise its risks [1].
